title: Great-grandmother Péche and her death in 1913
summary: Spelling of the great-grandmother's name, and the night she died when the child slept beside her.

blocks.x: And your great-grandmother was named Mimi Peche. P-E-C-H-E. Peche. Peche.
Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. Peche. She had been named for her mother.
Yeah. Your grand—great-grandmother's first name, the Mimi, what was that first name? How do you spell it?
Fetice. F-E-L. No. I-C-E. That's exactly it. Fetice. Yes. Because you see, you've got a hyphen over those E's. It's too childish.
Yes. Because the first name, because I wasn't the—I tried to guess at the name like that. I may not use that material either, but in case—I did want to mention what the grandmother—

That's right. After all, there's so few people can go back to the first generation. Can go back and tell that family. The family history, that's right. And my grandmother—my great-grandmother died in 1913. 1913. And mind you, I was in the bed with her. She had an abscess on the liver. Then when it braced there, all the blood came out through her mouth. And I was the one who went to call my grandmother and my aunt. She had—my aunt—grandmother had a sister there. The two of them were there. They were staying at night with her, but I slept with her. Yes. And I remember when this abscess burst, and when the blood and all this came out through her mouth, she—and she was dead. She didn't say another word after that. And they all called me baby when I was a child. Baby. Yes.

fours? That's all. About four, I think. I know, because she won't tell me. Yes, she won't tell. No.
